Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (SPICE, OMol25) and numerous baselines (MACE, eSEN, UMA, EquiformerV2, etc.) in both Conservative and Direct settings

Limited novelty of individual components: EAAS builds directly on eSCN's SO(2) reduction and on-the-fly attention applies FlashAttention's streaming softmax; combination is novel but incremental
Insufficient molecular dynamics validation with only one experiment (water RDF on 216 molecules); claim of 'high-fidelity reproduction' lacks evidence on complex systems or longer trajectories

Numerical stability concerns inadequately addressed: online softmax, rotation matrix inversions, and complex basis transformations (Eq. 19) could accumulate errors; no condition number analysis or stability bounds provided

No ablation studies isolating contributions of EAAS vs. fused kernel; Figure 3 tensor product benchmarks limited to 1000 operations; training throughput not evaluated

strengths: Rigorous mathematical foundation with complete proofs: Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.3 are correctly derived and well-presented, with thorough appendix derivations showing how pole sparsity of spherical harmonics enables sparse re-indexing.

Well-engineered systems contribution: The streaming on-the-fly equivariant attention kernel (Algorithm 1) thoughtfully adapts FlashAttention principles to equivariant networks with online softmax for numerical stability and SRAM-aware execution.
Significant practical impact: Achieves 20× speedup in sparse attention and linear O(|V|) memory scaling, enabling inference on previously infeasible 100k-atom systems on commodity GPUs.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets (SPICE, OMol25, OC20), extensive ablation studies (Table 4) isolating component contributions, scaling analysis with memory tracking, and molecular dynamics validation against experimental data.

Strong reproducibility: Detailed algorithmic descriptions, promised code release, complete hyperparameter specifications (Tables 9-10), extensive appendices addressing sensitivity analysis and implementation details.

Competitive accuracy maintenance: On SPICE, E2V2-Conservative achieves best-in-class energy MAE across most subsets; on OMol25 matches eSEN-small (1.27 vs 1.16 meV/atom) while dramatically improving scalability.
weaknesses: Moderate novelty with incremental advancement: The core node-centric factorization (Eq. 5) originates from E2Former (Li et al. 2025); this work primarily optimizes its implementation. Pole sparsity properties of spherical harmonics are classical mathematics. The contribution is systems-level engineering rather than algorithmic innovation.

Overstated sparsity narrative: EAAS still uses Clebsch-Gordan coefficients (Eq. 13) with deterministic sparsity patterns rather than eliminating dense computation; it avoids summing zeros but doesn't fundamentally transform the operation. Alone, EAAS provides only 1.5-3.6× speedup (Table 3); the dominant 20× gain comes from Triton kernel fusion.

Incompletely analyzed expressivity trade-offs: Replaces explicit value-path non-linearity (S² gating in EquiformerV2/eSEN) with attention-based non-linearity (Eq. 34-35) for efficiency. While labeled 'comparable accuracy' in Appendix D, results are mixed (Table 1 shows eSEN-Cons sometimes better on force MAE). The expressivity cost should be more prominent in main text.

Limited scope and applicability: Benefits materialize only for k ≥ 50-100 neighbors (Appendix E); performs comparably or worse for sparse graphs (k < 10). Specialized to 3D molecular systems with cutoff-based neighbors; unclear generalization to other graph domains. GPU optimizations tuned to H20; hardware generalization unexamined.

Experimental limitations and unfair comparisons: (1) Different baselines trained with different hyperparameters preventing fair comparison; (2) Some methods encounter OOM preventing head-to-head evaluation at large scales; (3) Table 5 conflates model differences with implementation choices by comparing Direct vs Conservative modes; (4) Appendix J shows sparse kernel ~100× slower than dense FlashAttention per-kernel throughput, limiting practical ceiling.

Insufficient molecular dynamics validation: Water RDF tested on single system; protein dynamics only 2ns with AlphaFold initialization, not truly validating force accuracy for diverse biomolecular systems. No comparison of MD trajectories to experimental reference data.

Incomplete limitation discussion: No systematic guidance on when to use E2Former-V2 vs alternatives. Memory-throughput-accuracy trade-offs not quantified. Failure modes and dataset characteristics enabling underperformance not discussed. Training-time efficiency absent.

Presentation issues: EAAS intuition (why axis-alignment helps) relegated to appendix; early sections mathematically dense; the '20×' speedup in Figure 1 refers only to sparse attention kernel, overstating full forward-pass gains. Notation inconsistency between ⊗ and @.

strengths: Addresses a critical practical bottleneck in equivariant GNNs by eliminating O(|E|) edge materialization, enabling 100k atom systems vs ~50k for prior methods
Strong mathematical foundation with rigorous derivations (Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3) and comprehensive proofs in appendices

Impressive experimental validation: 20× inference speedup, 16.9× memory reduction, scales to 100k atoms where prior methods OOM, with component ablation clearly showing necessity of both EAAS and Triton fusion
Physically validated via MD simulations (water RDF reproduction, 30k atom protein stability), confirming practical correctness
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, timing protocols, and implementation details; honest discussion of efficiency/expressivity trade-offs and neighbor-density sensitivity
Novel integration of EAAS algebraic sparsification with fused Triton kernels, adapting FlashAttention-style streaming to equivariant models
weaknesses: Claimed 'theoretical exactness' is overstated: non-linearity reorganization (Eqs. 34–35) represents an efficiency/expressivity trade-off vs EquiformerV2/eSEN's edge-level gating, not exact equivalence
Modest accuracy improvements: SPICE results inconsistent across subsets (some worsen), OMol25 competitive with eSEN-small but not clearly superior, OC20 comparable to baselines
Limited theoretical novelty: core factorization (Eq. 5) from E2Former; EAAS builds on existing SO(2) reductions (eSCN, EquiformerV2); main contribution is implementation optimization

Incomplete experimental coverage: no training time analysis, MD validation limited to 2 ns trajectories on single protein, synthetic FCC carbon benchmarks may not represent chemical diversity, missing failure-mode analysis
Irregular gather operations in Triton kernel substantially slower than dense FlashAttention (Table 12: ~2 TFLOPS vs ~38 TFLOPS), limiting absolute performance

Practical limitations underexplored: edge-centric methods faster for sparse graphs (k<10), custom GROMACS integration limits reproducibility, code not available at review time, GPU-specific (H20) results generalizability unclear
